Here's a tiny project picker that I thought I'd share. It's "hardcoded" to use ~/Projects for performance. Keep in mind that it hasn't been thoroughly tested and was mainly an ad hoc prototype for my own use :)


```lua
local projects = function(_, opts)
  local projects = {}
  local projects_dir = vim.fn.expand("~/Projects")

  for name, type in vim.fs.dir(projects_dir) do
    if type == "directory" then
      table.insert(projects, { text = name, dir = projects_dir .. '/' .. name })
    end
  end

  local choose = function(item)
    if not item then return end
    vim.fn.chdir(item.dir)

    -- Schedule to focus mini.files, as it doesn't otherwise.
    vim.schedule(function()
      require("mini.files").open(item.dir)
    end)
  end

  local preview = function(buf_id, item)
    if not item then return end

    local files = {}
    for name, type in vim.fs.dir(item.dir) do
      if type == "file" and not name:match("^%.") then
        table.insert(files, name)
      end
    end

    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, false, files)
  end

  local source = { items = projects, name = "Projects", choose = choose, preview = preview }
  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", { source = source }, opts or {})
  return MiniPick.start(opts)
end
```

Nice! This can be simplified, though:
- Instead of using CLI `find`, I'd recommend using `vim.fn.readdir()` (possibly together with `vim.fn.isdirectory()`). Or even `vim.fs.dir()` which already returns an iterator over entry name and its type (file, directory, etc.).
- `vim.cmd.cd(item.dir)` can be `vim.fn.chdir(item.dir)`. There are tiny differences (like the latter will automatically set the "most local" working directory), but otherwise they are the same. It's just usually cleaner to use function directly (if it exists) than command through `vim.cmd`.
- I am not really sure about motivation behind showing only files in preview. I'd say that just listing directory contents is more universally useful.

reply_data.body:
> @echasnovski Added your recommendations; let me know if there's more improvement that could be done. :)

Since you asked ( :) ), I'd personally wouldn't use `vim.fn.fnamemodify(item.dir .. '/' .. name, ":~:s?\\~/Projects/??")`. The `string.sub()` approach looks better (more explicit) here: `string.sub(item.dir .. '/' .. name, projects_dir:len() + 2)`. Or even just `name`.

By the way, I also realized (during trying this out, since I have the same kind directory in '~/repos'), that this is can be implemented as a wrapper for `MiniExtra.pickers.explorer()`. Here is what I'd use:

```lua
  MiniPick.registry.projects = function()
    local cwd = vim.fn.expand('~/Projects')
    local filter = function(data) return data.fs_type == 'directory' end
    local choose = function(item)
      vim.fn.chdir(item.path)
      vim.schedule(function() MiniFiles.open() end)
    end

    return MiniExtra.pickers.explorer({ cwd = cwd, filter = filter }, { source = { choose = choose } })
  end
```

reply_data.body:
> When I need to switch to another project, it's likely because I need to work on it directly, so having mini.files for renaming, editing, or moving files is necessary.

I tend to have both "work on the project" and "open file from that project for reference". The first one is covered by sessions and `MiniSessions.select()`, i.e. if there is "work on the project" then there should be session for it. The second one is also quite frequent (like take a look at specific Neovim source code file, for example) and which this new "projects" picker is intended to remedy. Up until now using `:Pick visit_paths` was enough (and even more straightforward as there is no need to pick the project first), but I'll try this one instead.

reply_data.body:
Where specifically do you want icons? If in "main" item list, then [`MiniExtra.pickers.explorer()` wrapper](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/1141#discussioncomment-10327131) already has it out of the box and I'd suggest just using it.

As a general suggestion for icons I'd recommend to make custom `show` which calls `MiniPick.default_show(buf_id, items, query, { show_icons = true })`. For it to work properly items should be [compatible with common item structure for paths](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/cf81e70e8f1fdc36a3c684efc45c4ee561285137/doc/mini-pick.txt#L252). In particular, either be tables with `path` being full path or plain strings (needs properly set `source.cwd` for relative paths to work).
